data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised $700M+ in total capital, including a recent majority recapitalization by Niobrara Capital and Prysm Capital. The target operates within a sector comprising 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers including Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems.

Valuation analysis is constrained by data limitations. Stage-progression methodology, applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for Growth-to-later-stage advancement, yields $840M. Peer-median analysis is inapplicable: while 12 same-sector peers exist, insufficient depth within identical stage and valuation tier filters out this method (minimum 3 datapoints required). Public-comp anchoring cannot be executed due to undisclosed target revenue; the sector median P/S multiple of 21.0x across three public semiconductors provides directional context only.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $714M to $966M, with a midpoint of $840M. This range reflects limited methodological overlap—only one applicable approach. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private transactions at equivalent stage and the lack of disclosed financial metrics (revenue, EBITDA) that would enable revenue or earnings multiple frameworks. Any refined valuation requires either proprietary financial disclosure or identification of narrower peer transactions.
